findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "find_skills" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Up to three skills from the aiqbench library that fit a task, each with a trust score, one line on what it adds for this task (why), the context cost in tokens,…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_skills · Private data: find_skills, get_skill · Public sink: find_skills, get_skill, install_command.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_skills · Private data: find_skills, get_skill · Public sink: find_skills, get_skill, install_command

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_skills" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
